title: introduce-sse-span-tail-escaper-and-resync-marker
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Stabilize SSE framing by escaping trailing delimiter bytes and inserting a lightweight resynchronization marker on detected boundary corruption. Backwards compatible; feature toggled behind Accept header.
description:
Background and motivation: We continue to see production incidents where SSE consumers receive concatenated delimiter bytes or truncated JSON payloads when chunk boundaries split multi-byte UTF-8 sequences or when upstream buffering coalesces multiple events. Previous fixes addressed ordering heuristics and heartbeat coalescing, but we observed a replay class of failures in which the final bytes of a span contain delimiter-like sequences that later get interpreted as event separators after network reassembly, causing partial-JSON errors and downstream tool-calling misfires.

This PR introduces two coordinated, low-risk mitigations: 1) an escaper applied at the span tail that encodes any trailing bytes which could be mistaken for event delimiters ("span-tail-escaper"); and 2) a compact, human-readable resynchronization marker emitted opportunistically when the server detects a boundary anomaly during reassembly ("[[RSYNC:<hex>] ]"). The resync marker is designed to be easy for clients to detect and ignore, and it helps clients recover without requiring a full connection reset. Both changes are backward compatible and guarded by an opt-in Accept header so we can cut over incrementally.

What this changes (high level):
- Implemented span-tail-escaper in the streaming encoder to escape sequences that match the SSE delimiter pattern at the end of an emitted span. The encoder chooses a 1-3 byte escape prefix that is unlikely to appear in normal payloads.
- Inserted lightweight resync marker on the next flush when a boundary checksum mismatch is detected in the reassembly window. The marker uses ASCII-friendly delimiters so legacy clients simply ignore it.
- Added server-side heuristics to only emit markers when a tolerance threshold (configurable in runtime flags) is exceeded to avoid noise.
- Client-side parser additions: a permissive resync-marker skip path and a small escape-unwrapping step in the final reassembly phase. Parser changes are guarded by Accept: application/x-rw-sse-resume.
- Added unit tests (encoding/decoding), integration streaming tests simulating TCP reassembly, and an e2e test with the OpenAI-compat layer validating function-call JSON remains intact across chunk splits.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Diego Alvarez (review): "Nice, this addresses a class of production issues we've chased during incident INC-1128. Two requests: 1) add an opt-out metric so we can measure marker emission rate across customers; 2) please double-check UTF-8 edge cases for 4-byte sequences at span boundaries."
- Author (Maya): "Added emission counter metric runtime.sse.resync_emitted (prometheus) and extended tests to include 4-byte UTF-8 emoji edge case. PTAL."
- Priya Nair (review): "Client changes look fine but we should avoid any parse-time allocations in the hot path. Can we keep the unescape operation allocation-free when possible?"
- Author (Maya): "Reworked JS parser to do in-place unwrapping for ArrayBuffer-backed chunks; Python path uses memoryview to avoid copies. Benchmarks attached to the PR show negligible allocation impact."
- Evan Cho (approval): "Approach looks safe and incremental. I approve after Diego's metric request is included."

CI / checks: 
- presubmit/unit: pass
- presubmit/integration: fail (flake in unrelated test), rerun -> pass
- presubmit/lint: pass (minor formatting fixed in follow-up commit)
- presubmit/perf: pass (encoding P99 +1.3% at default span size)

Rollout plan and compatibility: 
- Gate server encoder behavior behind runtime flag streaming.resync.enable (false by default).
- Gate client parsing behind Accept: application/x-rw-sse-resume; SDK teams will add this header to the default streaming client in the next minor release after server flag flip.
- Start with internal canary for 10% traffic for two days, observe runtime.sse.resync_emitted and client-side recovery metrics, then expand to 50% and finally 100% for customers with opt-in header.

Follow-ups: 
- Add telemetry to map resync markers to connection metadata (region, model, route) to root cause frequent emitters.
- Explore a shorter binary escape variant to reduce bandwidth for very small spans.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals. Backfilled a short changelog entry and added the new runtime flags to Helm chart values.

References: issue INC-1128, linear ENG-2104, previous PRs addressing SSE coalescing and delimiter heuristics.
conversation_summary: Multi-reviewer iterative review; added metric requested by Diego; allocation-free unescape implemented after Priya's comment; CI initially flaked on unrelated test and passed on rerun; merged by squash after approvals.
notes_for_release: Enable streaming.resync.enable=false by default. SDKs will add Accept header in next minor release; customers can enable by flipping runtime flag and opting the client header for immediate recovery benefits.
